answer.explanation: The alert compares a peak season with an annual average. The profile declared this seasonality, and till reports, stock and last year's peak all support it.
A grant of probate and the estate accounts explain the credits, and they came from the solicitors handling the estate.
The credit comes from the known employer, and the payslip and contract confirm it as an annual award.
The payments are small, regular, affordable and declared at onboarding, and the relationship is documented.
A documented sale of the customer's home explains the credit. The money came through solicitors and stayed in the customer's name.
The message from the sending bank is decisive, and the immediate onward payments fit the movement of stolen funds.

irregularity.note: Funds leave within hours through a money transfer business.
Large credits from individuals with no known link to the customer.
The explanation cannot be supported by any record.
A sending bank has reported that one of the payments was obtained by deception.
